newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain ready to host U.S. military planes.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain ready to host U.S. military planes.

text.p: Bahrain said on Sunday it had agreed to host United States military planes on the island but it was not clear whether the move was linked to the Iraqi crisis.
The state Gulf News Agency (GNA) quoted an official as saying Bahrain had "agreed to host a number of U.S. military planes on its territory".

Washington has moved up additional warplanes to the Gulf including radar-evading Stealth fighter-bombers now in Kuwait and B-52 bombers at the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia for possible military action against Iraq.
GNA said Bahrain's acceptance of U.S. warplanes on the island was in the framework of a defence cooperation pact with the United States. It gave no further details.
Officials said U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, who earlier arrived in Kuwait from Saudi Arabia, was due in Bahrain on Sunday and would speak at a news conference.
Bahrain is the administrative headquarters for the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet which operates an aircraft carrier battle group and other warships in the tense oil-rich region.

Bahrain was host to U.S. warplanes for about three months from last October when the carrier USS Independence left the Gulf and was replaced by the Nimitz. The carrier Carl Vinson is currently in the northern Gulf.
